profiles.normal: Relaxed, friendly, natural conversational rhythm, like chatting with his best friend.
profiles.excited: Excited and quick, words tumbling out a little faster, bright energy that comes from genuine delight, not shouting.
profiles.surprise: Genuinely caught off guard: a short beat, then the words come out slower with a rising, disbelieving tone.
profiles.confusion: Puzzled, a small hesitation, pitch rising at the end as if asking himself, natural pace.
profiles.sarcasm: Dry and understated, a little smile in the voice, deliberate pause before the key word.
profiles.embarrassment: Quietly embarrassed, a little hesitant, voice dropping slightly, a small awkward laugh, at a natural pace (not slow).
profiles.frustration: Controlled irritation, clipped words, an exasperated breath, never shouting.
profiles.curiosity: Leaning in, interested, light and open, a slight rise on questions.
profiles.confidence: Relaxed and assured, steady pace, sure of himself, a little swagger.
profiles.overconfidence: Breezy and very sure of himself about something he has wrong, explaining it like an obvious fact, quick and playful, emphasis on the big word.
profiles.nervousness: Nervous, quick little laugh, words a bit rushed, trying to sound fine.
profiles.disbelief: Flat disbelief, repeating it back as if it cannot be real, natural pace.
profiles.laughter: Laughing as he speaks, warm genuine chuckle breaking into the words.
profiles.whisper: Whispering, conspiratorial, leaning in, a little guilty.
profiles.serious: Calm and clear, sincere, explaining something he finally understands, natural pace.
profiles.storytelling: Animated storyteller, building the moment, varying pace, pausing before the punchline.
profiles.dramatic: A big, believable reaction, a gasp of air before the words, but still natural, not theatrical.
profiles.teasing: Smug and playful, teasing, a grin in the voice.
profiles.deadpan: Completely matter-of-fact and sincere, flat even pitch, no smile in the voice, no emphasis on any funny word, as if stating an obvious practical fact. Natural pace, does not pause for a laugh.
profiles.rationalising: Calm, articulate and slightly deliberate, choosing his words carefully, genuinely convinced his reasoning is sound. Earnest, a touch defensive, never smug, never jokey.
profiles.earnest: Genuine personal enthusiasm, a little quicker and brighter, like sharing something he really cares about with a friend. Believable adult excitement, not childish, not shouting.
profiles.research: Focused and quick, reading out a useful finding, professional words said naturally, a small lift of interest on the detail that supports his case.
profiles.fake_ill: Trying to sound unwell without much practice: slightly rough, lower, a little too careful and controlled, polite and formal, like he is managing his voice. Not a cartoon cough, not exaggerated; words still clearly articulated.
profiles.formal: Polite, controlled and slightly restrained, speaking to his manager, consciously managing his tone, professional and brief.
profiles.awkward: A small hesitation before the words, slightly too casual, fishing for information while pretending not to, a little stilted. No stammering, no laugh.
profiles.under_breath: Quiet, lower volume, talking to himself rather than to anyone, conversational and dry, not a whisper; every consonant still clearly articulated.
profiles.defeated: Tired and quietly resigned, low energy, mildly defeated, no outrage, just accepting a small disaster that became a big one.
profiles.deflated: Quiet and a little disappointed, softer, almost sincere, a small sigh of a man who liked his own idea.

usage: Each script line may set 'voice' (a performance style: a profile here for Ryan, a Chatterbox STYLE for others), 'direction' (free text) or 'delivery'; otherwise its emotion picks a profile.
